title: Find equivalent ratios with a ratio table

lesson.title: Ratio Tables: Making Equal Ratios

steps.say: You already know how to write a ratio, like three to two, and you know how to make equivalent fractions by multiplying the top and the bottom by the same number. Today we use that same idea to fill in a ratio table, so we can answer questions like: if this recipe works for a small batch, what do I need for a bigger batch?

Here is our recipe. To make trail mix for a hike up Grouse Mountain, Ms. Yuanyuan mixes three scoops of almonds with two scoops of dried cranberries. That is the ratio three to two. A ratio table just lines those two numbers up in columns so we can grow them together.

visual.caption: One batch: 3 scoops almonds to 2 scoops cranberries

steps.say: Here is the one rule. Whatever you multiply the top number by, you must multiply the bottom number by the very same thing. Multiply both by two: three times two is six, and two times two is four. So six to four is the same mix, just a double batch. Multiply both by three: three times three is nine, and two times three is six. Nine to six is a triple batch. Same taste every time, because both numbers grew by the same amount.

visual.caption: Times 2, then times 3 — both rows grow together

steps.say: Now watch a mistake that is really easy to make. Some people look at three to two and think, I will just add one to each, and write four to three. But that is not the same mix. Let us check it. In three to two, the almonds are one and a half times the cranberries. In four to three, the almonds are only about one point three times the cranberries. The trail mix got more cranberry-ish. Ratios grow by multiplying, never by adding.

visual.caption: Adding 1 to each changes the mix — multiplying keeps it the same

steps.say: Let us finish one together. Ms. Yuanyuan needs twelve scoops of almonds for a big class hike. How many scoops of cranberries? Ask yourself, three times what gives twelve? Three times four is twelve. So multiply the bottom by four too: two times four is eight. She needs eight scoops of cranberries. And check: is three to two the same as twelve to eight? Yes, because both numbers were multiplied by four.

visual.caption: Times 4 on both rows: 12 almonds needs 8 cranberries

steps.say: So remember: in a ratio table, both numbers ride the same multiplying elevator. Multiply, never add.

lesson.answer: To make an equivalent ratio, multiply BOTH numbers by the same number — never add.

practice.question: At the farmers market in Kelowna, apples cost four dollars for every five apples. Draw a small two-row ratio table with the headings 'Apples' and 'Dollars', and start it with five apples and four dollars. Fill in the next two columns by multiplying both numbers by two, and then by three. How many dollars do fifteen apples cost?
practice.answer: Times two gives ten apples for eight dollars. Times three gives fifteen apples for twelve dollars. So fifteen apples cost twelve dollars.
